applicabilityBasis.summary: USDFC is a general dollar-pegged token minted by users against FIL collateral. Official documentation advertises EIP-3009/x402 payment flows, so payment use cannot be dismissed. Redemption returns oracle-priced FIL, net of fees and subject to system collateralization, rather than a demonstrated issuer obligation to pay a fixed amount of national currency or a bank deposit. The operator terms expressly separate the interface from third-party USDFC Trove contracts. The payment-use limb is present but the statutory issuer/monetary-redemption limb is unresolved.

genius.notes: The February 20, 2025 terms identify SFF Holdings S.A., incorporated in Panama, as the interface owner. They expressly say users are not buying or selling assets from it and it does not operate the underlying smart contracts. This is not enough to identify it as USDFC token issuer; issuerEntity and issuerDomicile are intentionally omitted. Public reserve disclosure means protocol collateral/vault transparency, not confirmation of GENIUS-eligible reserves or reserve sufficiency. No public issuer 1:1 cash/deposit redemption policy or monthly independent reserve attestation was located in the checked disclosures; documented collateral/token redemption mechanics still exist. The Act remains pre-effective under the October 7, 2026 regime review: the September 30 SCRC procedural interim rule is not the comprehensive final-regulation trigger. General DASP restrictions begin July 18, 2028; foreign-offer lawful-order requirements follow Act effectiveness. No approval, unlawful status, whole-protocol exemption or registered foreign exception is inferred.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official pending application, foreign registration/comparability decision, or issuer-announced GENIUS intent naming USDFC, Secured Finance and SFF Holdings S.A. was found in the opened implementation materials, NYDFS directory, protocol/legal disclosures and exact-name regulator-domain searches. General rulemaking pages are not comprehensive issuer approval directories; this is a dated bounded negative-evidence finding, not proof that no confidential filing exists or a finding of unlawful issuance.
